root_cause_label: Oversimplified Strategy: Quadratic Gradient Instead of Path Tracing
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent failed to recognize that the image is a 3D path-traced scene and instead attempted to approximate it with simple quadratic color gradient formulas, which cannot achieve the required 0.99 similarity.
t_err_evidence: Step 2: Agent writes a solid light-blue image without first understanding the structure of the reference image, acting on the false premise that the first pixel color (159, 197, 255) characterizes the whole image.
t_commit_evidence: Step 12: Agent writes the final C program using quadratic gradient formulas derived from sparse pixel samples, committing to a strategy that cannot produce a 0.99 similarity match to a 3D path-traced scene with geometric structure (sphere, floor, sky).
trigger_explanation: At step 2, the agent acts on an unverified assumption that the image is a simple solid color (based on only the first pixel), and later at step 12 assumes a quadratic polynomial model can replicate a 3D ray-traced scene despite sampling data showing three clearly distinct regions (blue sky, dark red sphere, gray floor) indicating complex geometric rendering.
forewarning_evidence: Step 5: Center pixel (1200,900) is dark red (51,10,10), drastically different from the top-left light blue (159,197,255), clearly indicating structured scene geometry. Steps 7 and 11 reveal gray pixels (152,152,152) at the bottom, confirming three distinct regions (sky, sphere, floor) consistent with a 3D rendered scene — not a gradient.
